title: Context Tenacity Stress Harness (8k/32k/128k)
summary: Working notes and experimental harness for measuring context robustness (8k/32k/128k) under retrieval-heavy workloads and artificial attention-drain injection. Focus is on quantifying graceful degradation, truncation interaction with retrieval reranking, and KV-cache coherence during backpressure.
objectives: 1) Produce reproducible stress scenarios that expose truncation and KV-cache divergence across sequence lengths. 2) Measure token retention and hallucination rate when retrieval latency and partial replies occur. 3) Validate mitigations (prefetch, adaptive chunking, prefix-pruning).
test_matrix: Models: open-variants + Redwood-verified builds (fp16 and 4-bit quant). Sequence lengths: 8k, 32k, 128k. Retrieval modes: synchronous fetch, async prefetch, delayed (simulated high-latency). Load shapes: single-stream, bursty 50QPS, sustained 200QPS on Dedicated pool. Failure modes: truncated retrieval documents, partial prefix KV warm-start, attention-sink payloads (100k token irrelevant prefix).
harness_setup: Runner: local harness v0.9.2 (python). Env: dedicated dev-pool g4dn-equivalent for parity with CI. Key toggles: RETRIEVAL_PREFETCH=true|false, KV_PREFILL=none|partial|full, ATTENTION_SINK=0|1. Logging: token-level diff, generation probability traces, kv-cache hit/miss timestamps. See reproducer_commands for exact invocations.
prompt_samples: User question: Summarize the attached set of legal clauses and list obligations by party. Retrieval includes 12 docs, one doc is intentionally truncated at 2k tokens to simulate truncation.
Conversation: System: You are a concise assistant. Context: [RETRIEVED_DOCS]. User: Draft a short email to explain the change and next steps.
Long chain prompt: <100k random noise> + Relevant passage + 'Given the passage above, extract the three action items.'
observations:
- 8k: generally stable; truncation occurs predictably when retrieval result length plus prompt > limit. KV-cache warm starts reduce latency by ~18% on repeated queries.
- 32k: divergence appears when retrieval latency > 300ms; model sometimes repeats retrieval metadata instead of content (indexing artifact). Hallucination rate up ~2.1% on our eval set.
- 128k: attention-sink injection (100k irrelevant prefix) causes token rejection behavior in fp16 builds leading to early truncation; 4-bit quant variants show higher instability in kv-cache alignment leading to 0.8% generation nondeterminism across runs.
- Across lengths, async prefetch reduces perceived latency but increases chance of stale doc inclusion if retrieval reranker updated mid-call (observed 4 cases).
metrics_summary:
Measured metrics (median over 3 runs):
- Token retention (percent of ground-truth retrieval tokens used): 8k=99.6%, 32k=95.2%, 128k=88.3%.
- KV-cache hit rate on repeated prompt: 8k=92%, 32k=85%, 128k=73%.
- Latency p95 generation (end-to-end): 8k=210ms, 32k=480ms, 128k=1.9s.
- Hallucination proxy (BLEU-based divergence on golden extractions): 8k=0.9%, 32k=2.1%, 128k=6.7%.
attention_sink_tests: Method: prepend large unrelated token blocks (synthetic tokens with high entropy) before relevant context. Goal: test attention window management and whether runtime prunes irrelevant prefixes. Findings: runtime currently keeps attention over entire input unless prefix-pruning enabled; enabling prefix-pruning at 64k window reduced p95 latency by 12% and hallucination by 1.5% at 128k but increased partial-answer truncation for very long retrieved docs. Note: prefix-pruning introduces potential non-determinism when combined with KV prefill.
truncation_behavior: Observed two truncation classes: hard-truncation (drop trailing tokens, deterministic) and graceful-trim (model rewrites prompt to fit, sometimes omits 'context end' markers). Graceful-trim occurred mostly in quantized builds under high QPS; hard-truncation in fp16 only when token buffer exceeded memory thresholds. Regression threshold: any change causing >1% increase in graceful-trim count at 32k baseline should block rollout.
failure_cases_examples:
1) Retrieval-doc split: a single long doc was split across two retrieval results; when assembled client-side it exceeded sequence budget and model dropped the end of the doc (seen in 32k runs).
2) Partial KV warm-start: when KV_PREFILL=partial and prefetch delayed, early tokens were generated using stale kv snapshot and led to looped token output until fallback triggered.
3) Attention-sink with rerank flip: reranker updated ordering after initial prefetch; model continued to use outdated top-1 doc causing incorrect answer (seen 4/30 128k runs).
reproducer_commands:
1) Baseline run (32k): python harness/run_eval.py --model redwood/open-32k-fp16 --seq_len 32768 --retrieval_mode sync --qps 50 --testset tests/long_retrieval.json
2) Attention-sink (128k): python harness/run_eval.py --model redwood/open-128k-4bit --seq_len 131072 --retrieval_mode async --attention_sink 100000 --kv_prefill partial --qps 20
3) Prefetch race sim: ./scripts/sim_prefetch_race.sh --iterations 100 --delay-ms 350 --model redwood/open-64k-fp16
recommended_actions:
- Short term: enforce deterministic truncation policy at serving layer and emit explicit truncated-doc warnings in response metadata.
- Medium term: add a pre-commit KV-check that verifies prefill snapshot freshness vs reranker version and forces sync fetch if mismatch.
- Long term: expose adaptive prefix-pruning knob in Optimize with safe defaults per sequence length (64k for >64k deployments).
- Also: add a regression test (CI) that runs attention-sink scenario on PRs that touch tokenization or kv-cache code paths.
open_questions:
- What's acceptable production nondeterminism threshold for Dedicated customers at 128k? (ops/product tradeoff).
- Should we prioritize prefetch freshness (strong consistency) or latency for PLG users?
- How to quantify user-visible impact of graceful-trim vs hard-truncation for downstream chains?
next_steps: 1) Share with runtime owners (tag SRE and serving-runtime) and file follow-up JIRA for deterministic truncation fix. 2) Add two CI cells: attention-sink smoke and retriever-freshness check. 3) Run extended 128k overnight soak (24h) on Dedicated pool and collect token-diff traces for flaky case triage.
notes_to_self:

- Watch for cross-talk with console rollouts feature (can change routing mid-test).
- Consider a small user study for 'perceived truncation annoyance' with solutions engineering customers.
